newsitem.title: UK: London shares stuck in narrow range, await Wall St.
newsitem.headline: London shares stuck in narrow range, await Wall St.

text.p: UK shares were little changed on Friday as a cocktail of political and economic uncertainties combined to keep many institutional investors on the sidelines.
"We desperately need some good news. But the(UK corporate) reporting season is over and there just isn't anything to create any enthusiasm," the head of trading at a major brokerage said.
"It's been another extremely boring day," he added.
The FTSE 100, which has been trading in a 20-30 point daily range all week, was up 2.7 points to 4,301.6.

The FTSE's range was a mere 11 points by 1305 GMT as many fund managers stayed away ahead of the May 1 British election which the opposition Labour party, with a 20 percentage point lead in opinion polls, is favoured to win.
Some market watchers believe Labour may discover a gaping hole in Britain's finances and be tempted to raise corporate taxes in order to plug the gap.
A Labour Chancellor is also expected to agree to Bank of England repeated requests for higher interest rates in order to prevent a future spike in UK inflation.

"The pace of economic expansion will probably be too fast by Bank and Treasury officials advising an incoming Chancellor which is one reason why we expect base rates to be raised soon after the first post-election monetary meeting on May 7," analysts at UBS Global Research said in its latest global equities research paper.
Fears that Wall Street may also be on the verge of another setback continued to weigh on market sentiment, dealers said.
"People still think the Dow has not seen the bottom. The question is how far will the Dow fall," one trader said.
U.S. blue chips are forecast to open higher on Friday, boosted by higher-than-expected third-quarter earnings news from software giant Microsoft Corp.
Standard Chartered a star performer on Thursday, was up another 26p to 891p following an upgrade from Schroder Securities yesterday.

British Telecommunications Plc rose 4p to 446-1/2 after the confirmation of a global alliance with Telefonica de Espana -- a deal which opens up the potentially lucrative Latin American telecoms market.
